title: Things to Do in Varkala: Cliffs, Beaches, Temples & Slow Days
seoTitle: Things to Do in Varkala: Cliff, Beaches & Yoga | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Varkala: sunset on the North Cliff, Papanasham beach and the Janardanaswamy Temple, Sivagiri Mutt, Black Beach and Odayam, Kappil where backwater meets sea, Ponnumthuruthu island, Anjengo Fort, surfing, yoga and Ayurveda.
dek: Red laterite cliffs above the Arabian Sea on Kerala's southern coast, with cafés along the edge, a sacred beach below and backwaters just inland.
searchIntent: Couples, solo travellers and wellness seekers planning two days to a week in Varkala.

hero.alt: Red cliffs above the beach at Varkala

intro: Varkala, about 50 km north of Thiruvananthapuram, is the only place on the Kerala coast where cliffs rise directly above the beach. The red laterite North Cliff is lined with cafés, guesthouses, yoga studios and Ayurveda centres, while the beach below, Papanasham, is sacred to Hindus, who perform rituals for their ancestors in the sea.

The things to do in Varkala are relaxed: watching the sunset from the cliff, swimming and surfing, visiting the ancient Janardanaswamy Temple and Sivagiri Mutt, walking to quieter beaches, and paddling through the backwaters to Ponnumthuruthu island. Many visitors come for yoga courses and Ayurvedic treatments.
Two days is enough for the sights; many people stay a week or more. October to March is the best time; the monsoon brings rough seas and erosion on the cliff.

See Sivagiri Mutt, the samadhi of Sree Narayana Guru

items.name: Watch sunset from the North Cliff
body: The North Cliff's walkway runs along the edge above the sea, lined with cafés and shops. Sunset here, with the sky reflected on the wet sand below, is Varkala's defining experience. Keep well back from the edge; parts of the cliff are eroding, and some sections have been fenced off.

facts.Good to know: Stay back from the eroding edge

items.name: Swim at Papanasham beach
body: Papanasham, below the cliff, is the main beach. Its name refers to the washing away of sins, and pilgrims come to perform rituals for ancestors, especially on Karkidaka Vavu in July or August. Lifeguards patrol parts of the beach; swim only between the flags, as currents can be strong.

items.name: Walk to Black Beach and Odayam
body: North of the cliff, Black Beach, named for its patches of dark mineral sand, is quieter. Further on, Odayam beach is secluded and good for long walks.

items.name: See Kappil beach
body: Kappil, about 9 km north, is where a backwater lake meets the sea, with a strip of sand between them. A small bridge and boating on the lake make it a peaceful stop, especially at sunset.

items.name: Take a surf lesson
body: Varkala's beach breaks are good for beginners, and several surf schools rent boards and offer lessons in the dry season.

items.name: Visit the Janardanaswamy Temple
body: The Janardanaswamy Temple, dedicated to Vishnu, stands on a hill near Papanasham and is believed to be about 2,000 years old. It is an important pilgrimage site; entry to the inner temple is restricted to Hindus, and a dress code applies.

items.name: See Sivagiri Mutt
body: Sivagiri Mutt, on a hill in Varkala town, was founded by the social reformer Sree Narayana Guru, whose samadhi is here. The Sivagiri pilgrimage in late December and early January draws huge crowds.

facts.Best time: Late December to early January for the pilgrimage

items.name: Visit Anjengo Fort
body: Anjengo (Anchuthengu) Fort, about 15 km south, was built by the British East India Company in the 1690s and is one of its earliest settlements in Kerala. A lighthouse nearby can be climbed for views, and there is an old cemetery.

items.name: Canoe to Ponnumthuruthu island
body: Ponnumthuruthu, the golden island, is a small island in the Anjengo backwaters with an old temple, reached by canoe from Nedunganda. The trip through mangroves and quiet water is a lovely half day.

items.name: See the Varkala Tunnel
body: The Varkala Tunnel, built in the 1870s and 1880s, carries a canal of the old waterway between Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram through a hill. It is a curiosity of Kerala's canal history.

items.name: Join a yoga class or course
body: Many studios on the cliff offer drop-in classes and multi-week teacher-training courses. Check teachers' credentials and read reviews.

items.name: Take an Ayurveda treatment
body: Varkala has many Ayurvedic centres, from massage clinics to residential treatment programmes. Choose centres with qualified doctors and certification, especially for longer treatments.

items.name: Eat at the cliff cafés
body: Cliff cafés serve fresh seafood, Kerala dishes and international food. Choose your fish from the display in the evening and have it grilled. Try a Kerala breakfast of puttu and kadala in town.

byTraveller.text: A cliff-view room, sunset cafés, Kappil at dusk and a canoe trip to Ponnumthuruthu.
Yoga in the morning, surf lessons, and a friendly café scene.
A week-long Ayurveda programme with yoga and quiet beach walks.

oneDay: Visit the Janardanaswamy Temple early, then swim at Papanasham. Walk north to Black Beach and Odayam, have lunch on the cliff, and drive to Kappil in the late afternoon before returning to the North Cliff for sunset.
tips: Varkala Sivagiri railway station is a few kilometres from the cliff; Thiruvananthapuram airport is about an hour away.
Dress modestly in town and at temples; beachwear belongs on the beach.
Cliff paths are unlit in places; carry a torch at night.
Many businesses close during the monsoon.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Varkala?
faqs.a: Watch sunset from the North Cliff, swim at Papanasham, visit the Janardanaswamy Temple and Sivagiri Mutt, walk to Black Beach and Odayam, see Kappil, canoe to Ponnumthuruthu and try surfing, yoga or Ayurveda.

faqs.q: Is it safe to swim in Varkala?
faqs.a: In calm conditions and between the lifeguard flags. Currents can be strong, and the sea is rough in the monsoon.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Varkala?
faqs.a: Two days for the sights; a week or more for yoga or Ayurveda.
